R01 · round 1

Disclosed v1 controls

Status
verified_main
Turning point
Yes — research direction changed

Hypothesis

Constructive arithmetic circuits can reproduce every disclosed-v1 truth-table output exactly in the challenge XAG metric.

Independent variable

Arithmetic construction for each disclosed control.

Permitted data

  • Disclosed v1 archive and functions.
  • Tracked arithmetic source, circuits, predictions, and exhaustive tests.

Frozen controls

  • A=x+y at 37 gates.
  • B=abs(x-y) at 49 gates.
  • C=x*y at 168 gates.
  • D=x²+y² at 127 gates.

Outcome

Four deterministic circuits and committed prediction tables reproduce the disclosed controls at 37, 49, 168, and 127 reachable gates.

Decision

Retain the four arithmetic solutions as disclosed controls and constructive upper bounds only.

Insight

The controls establish a semantic and serialization baseline, not a blind-learning result or minimality certificate.

Limitations

  • The functions were disclosed.
  • The round predates the later immutable official-record infrastructure.

Next pivot

Separate disclosed-control reproduction from the genuinely blind benchmark and freeze the evidence tracks.

Turning point
Yes — research direction changed

Hypothesis

A frozen reblind protocol can prevent disclosed-control leakage and sealed-data feedback while preserving reproducible visible-only selection.

Independent variable

Evidence and information-access boundary, not an algorithm.

Permitted data

  • Tracked protocol, commitments, nonidentifying manifest metadata, and synthetic fixtures.
  • No public training rows, sealed rows, private digests, or evaluator feedback.

Frozen controls

  • Two frozen public baseline methods.
  • Accuracy-first-then-gates comparison.
  • Visible-only selection before sealed confirmation.
  • Five-minute per-cell timeout and complete terminal retention.

Outcome

The repository gained a content-addressed visible/sealed protocol, bounded runner contract, and terminal-evidence checks without mounting the public archive.

Decision

Freeze the public-visible and sealed boundaries before proposing a learner; do not execute absent studies.

Insight

Benchmark identity, folds, baselines, metrics, and timeout must be fixed before algorithm selection.

Limitations

  • This round froze contracts and tests but executed no public or sealed algorithm cell.

Next pivot

Implement synthetic-only candidate and exact-resynthesis methods behind the frozen public gate.

Turning point

Hypothesis

A shared complemented-edge Care-BDD can complete unseen branches deterministically while preserving every observed row.

Independent variable

Care-set completion policy and bounded variable-order search.

Permitted data

  • Tracked contracts and generated synthetic partial and complete tables.
  • Disclosed controls only as labelled controls; no public or sealed rows.

Frozen controls

  • Reuse-sibling completion with zero-fill as an ablation.
  • Five visible folds.
  • Four-member beam and at most 32 unique order evaluations.
  • Training consistency and exhaustive completed-table/XAG equality.

Outcome

Four timing calibrations passed, including two 32-evaluation repeats at 63.161153 and 65.831928 seconds with exhaustive equality over 2^20 rows; the memory wrapper failed.

Decision

Integrate the synthetic-verified Care-BDD method, but defer every public claim until the reviewed archive is supplied.

Insight

The method is exact and comfortably within the local time budget, but synthetic timing does not establish public accuracy.

Limitations

  • No public row, official Julia record, or trustworthy peak-memory measurement was available.

Next pivot

Integrate with bounded exact resynthesis, then inspect how the 32-evaluation scheduler allocates its search.

Turning point

Hypothesis

Bounded exact synthesis can replace a local XAG window with a strictly smaller exact window under frozen resource bounds.

Independent variable

Exact local gate bound in a deterministic SAT encoding.

Permitted data

  • Generated complete Boolean tables and generated circuits.
  • Tracked contracts and disclosed controls only; no public or sealed rows.

Frozen controls

  • At most six cut inputs, 128 cuts, and 64 solver calls.
  • One 285-second inner deadline inside the 300-second runner cap.
  • Challenge-native reachable XOR-plus-AND gates.
  • Cut and whole-circuit exhaustive equivalence after reinsertion.

Outcome

Exact fixtures recovered zero-, one-, and two-gate solutions and reduced 3-to-1 and 4-to-2 gates; deadline and solver-interruption paths remained censored.

Decision

Integrate bounded SAT as an exact local tool; keep Timeout and Unknown censored and make no whole-circuit minimality claim.

Insight

Small exact rewrites work, but solver interruption and deadline outcomes must stay distinct from UNSAT.

Limitations

  • No independent DRAT checker was pinned.
  • The development fixtures are synthetic tool evidence, not public benchmark cells.

Next pivot

Compose the tool only after an eligible exact candidate exists, and stop on censored or non-improving outcomes.

Hypothesis

Integrating Care-BDD and bounded SAT without changing either contract will expose the next high-value optimization bottleneck.

Independent variable

Integration and read-only scheduler audit; no third algorithm.

Permitted data

  • Tracked source, contracts, synthetic fixtures, and disclosed controls.
  • No public, sealed, private, remote, or HPC data.

Frozen controls

  • Care-BDD five folds, reuse-sibling policy, and 32 order evaluations.
  • Bounded SAT six-input and 285-second limits.
  • Internal equivalence and official verification remain separate.

Outcome

Care-BDD and SAT commands integrated, one false verifier pass was corrected to not_run, and the synthetic scheduling audit completed in 70.273820 seconds.

Decision

Correct the false verifier state and test a fairer order scheduler as the next single-variable hypothesis.

Insight

The 32-evaluation search allocated adjacent neighbors 19/5/0/0 across the beam, revealing a coverage artifact.

Limitations

  • The scheduler audit was one synthetic timing cell.
  • The integration created no public accuracy or official-Julia result.

Next pivot

Hold all other controls fixed and interleave order candidates fairly across the four beam members.

Hypothesis

Interleaving adjacent order candidates 6/6/6/6 across the four retained beam members will improve the frozen synthetic BlindScore.

Independent variable

Candidate scheduling allocation only.

Permitted data

  • Tracked 20-input synthetic calibration and source.
  • No public, sealed, private, Julia, or remote data.

Frozen controls

  • Legacy 19/5/0/0 scheduler versus fair 6/6/6/6 scheduler.
  • Same 20-input, 21-output, 104857-row synthetic fixture.
  • Same folds, completion, score, beam, and 32-evaluation budget.

Outcome

Legacy and fair rank-zero results both scored 0/104857 exact rows and 36084 gates; two fair repeats were deterministic and two bounded diagnostics were retained as invalid.

Decision

Reject fair scheduling for promotion and pivot from coverage allocation to label-aware order construction.

Insight

Fair allocation fixed the coverage defect but rank-zero quality remained byte-identical, so the next method must change the order signal.

Limitations

  • Manual runs lacked the full claim-grade runner envelope.
  • The two bounded diagnostics were INVALID_METRICS and official verification was not run.

Next pivot

Derive a fold-local order from exact label conflicts while keeping all completion and scoring controls fixed.

Hypothesis

A fold-local greedy order minimizing differently labelled prefix conflicts will improve exact-row CV over the fair fixed-order beam.

Independent variable

Fold-local label-aware global variable order.

Permitted data

  • Tracked 20-input synthetic fixture and fold-local labels.
  • No public, sealed, private, Julia, SAT, TN, or HPC resource.

Frozen controls

  • Fair fixed-order beam at 36084 gates.
  • Same five folds, 104857-row synthetic fixture, completion policy, and Rust backend.
  • Exact-row accuracy first and reachable gates only after a tie.

Outcome

The corrected fair control used 36084 gates; two byte-identical greedy repeats used 34917 gates, while all three remained 0/104857 exact rows.

Decision

Advance only to public-candidate consideration, then pivot toward per-output support selection because exact-row CV stayed zero.

Insight

The label-aware order reduced gates but not exact-row CV; gate-only gains at zero exact-row generalization are secondary.

Limitations

  • Every valid cell ended VERIFIER_NOT_RUN.
  • No public bundle, official Julia record, or sealed result was used.

Next pivot

Reduce irrelevant-variable overfitting by selecting a separate conflict-free projected support for each output.

Hypothesis

Evidence-bound verifier, promotion, skills, and report infrastructure can turn branch research into a navigable deliverable without overstating scientific status.

Independent variable

Proof and navigation infrastructure, not an optimization algorithm.

Permitted data

  • Tracked public repository evidence and exact historical commit blobs.
  • No public archive, sealed rows, private custodian digests, or remote compute.

Frozen controls

  • Truthful runner verifier states.
  • Fail-closed Julia wrapper and immutable official record schema.
  • Track-specific promotion ceilings and replayable current request.
  • Canonical offline report source with structural claims and exact evidence locators.

Outcome

The current all-none blind-visible request replays to blocked for four missing evidence classes; the highest legal next step remains freeze_candidate.

Decision

Publish only the replayed blocked state; route the next work to the public visible gate rather than claiming promotion.

Insight

A human-readable report is useful only when its conclusion is derived from structural proof state and preserves failed, invalid, equal, superseded, and blocked records.

Limitations

  • The public bundle and sealed evidence remain outside the repository.
  • Branch algorithms are referenced as historical evidence and were not silently merged into mainline.

Next pivot

Approve and freeze the R2 public-candidate integration decision before obtaining the reviewed public bundle; only then run the baseline plus visible-only matrix, before any sealed access.
